title: Her sister books her to Australia with Red Norvo
summary: Working in San Francisco, Humes was told by her sister Dorothy that she had been booked for Australia with Red Norvo and had to go. She mentions friendship with Mildred Bailey and Norvo's wife Eve.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I was working up in San Francisco, and Dorothy, that's my sister, she called me and she said, 'well I just booked you down in Austrialia'. I said, 'well you must be going down there to sing because I ain't going way down there'. She said, 'yes you are now. You have to go'. I said, 'who am I going with?' She said, Red Norvo. And I said, 'shucks, I ain't going down there'. She said, 'yes you are because I told them on television that you was coming and now you got to go'. When I came on back here I went to see Bailey and we got it all straightened out.
Well you were friends with Mildred too, weren't you?
Yeah, and I was friends with . . .

Yes. I got the last letter she wrote me. She was so sweet.
